svg.title: Five-Step Brokerage Launch Roadmap
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-01-launch-roadmap; chapter number: 1; title: Five-Step Brokerage Launch Roadmap; subtitle: From niche selection to a funded float, per Matt Krause and The Finance Pro; chart type: process_flow; caption: Krause launches on hard freight, files authority for roughly $2,500 to $4,500 all-in, runs a stack near $300 a month, and funds the float before booking volume.; assumptions note: Dollar figures are attributed practitioner claims. Startup cost excludes training. The $40,000 float assumes 10 loads a week, as Krause frames it.; note: Sources - Matt Krause (afV63okbAMs, bP4Dnpd58PE) and The Finance Pro (29d2gRCN8Ng).; stages: step: 01; label: Pick a hard-freight niche; value: Step 1; detail: Chase steel, lumber and machinery, which Krause calls 1/4 of the work for the same money. Satellite recon shows white rectangles for lumber, gray cylinders for steel coils and yellow shapes for machinery.; step: 02; label: File authority and bond; value: Step 2; detail: The $300 FMCSA fee, BMC-84 premium, BOC-3, $46 UCR, LLC and contingent cargo run about $2,500 to $3,500, or $3,500 to $4,500 with weaker credit.; step: 03; label: Stand up the tech stack; value: Step 3; detail: Load board ~$150, vetting tool $50-$100, TMS ~$25 or free, phone $30. Total ~$300 a month, covered by one $400-margin load.; step: 04; label: Build the prospect list; value: Step 4; detail: Look for 3+ dock doors with trailers and a careers page posting logistics openings, then star 50 prospects before dialing. Who is on the list matters more than how many.; step: 05; label: Fund the float; value: Step 5; detail: At 10 loads a week a new desk is $40,000 out of pocket by week four. With $10K of monthly overhead at $200 per load, break-even is 50 loads a month.
